status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 one of the three recommendations is law and nearly operative, and the other two are not. Public Law 119-21 (enacted 2025-07-04, title VII section 70411) added section 25F to the Internal Revenue Code, a federal credit for cash donations to scholarship-granting organizations that applies to taxable years ending after 2026-12-31 and differs from the Mandate's example bill: the credit is capped at $1,700 per taxpayer per year, states must opt in, and scholarships go to students in households at or below 300 percent of area median gross income (26 U.S.C. 25F as reproduced by Cornell's Legal Information Institute). Treasury and the IRS published temporary and proposed regulations on 2026-10-02 (temporary rules effective 2026-12-01; comments on the proposal due 2026-12-01), and a States Newsroom report of 2026-10-01 cited an IRS count of 30 states that had opted in, with governors in Hawaii, Minnesota, New Mexico and Oregon saying they will not. The D.C. Opportunity Scholarship Program continues under its existing law; a bill to reauthorize it through fiscal year 2032 (H.R. 5181, introduced 2025-09-08) does not appear to change its income limits. Executive Order 14191 (2025-01-29) directed ED to issue guidance on using federal formula funds for school choice within 60 days and the Defense and Interior Departments to review options and submit plans within 90 days for military and Bureau of Indian Education families; ED has issued letters to chief state school officers on using Title I funds for school choice (its pages carry no issue date), but no Defense or Interior plan was found and no federal education savings account for D.C., military or tribal-school students was found (the order does not mention education savings accounts).

timeline.event: Executive Order 14191 directs ED to issue guidance within 60 days on using federal formula funds for K-12 school choice and to make education freedom a grant priority, and directs the Defense and Interior Secretaries to review options and submit plans within 90 days for military-connected and Bureau of Indian Education families; the text does not mention education savings accounts.
ED invites FY2025 applications for the D.C. Opportunity Scholarship Program under its existing authorizing law.

Public Law 119-21, the reconciliation act, adds section 25F to the Internal Revenue Code (title VII section 70411): a credit equal to cash donations to qualifying scholarship granting organizations, capped at $1,700 per taxable year, for taxable years ending after 2026-12-31; a state or the District of Columbia may opt in and certify a list of organizations; scholarships go to students in households at or below 300 percent of area median gross income. The Education Commission of the States describes the same design.
timeline.source: U.S. Code (26 U.S.C. 25F, via Cornell Legal Information Institute)

timeline.event: Rep. Foxx introduces H.R. 5181, the SOAR Act Improvements Act, which would reauthorize the D.C. Opportunity Scholarship Program through fiscal year 2032, allow pre-kindergarten use, allow renewal of grants without new competition, and change accreditation and testing rules; the text does not appear to change student income limits.

ED publishes final supplemental grant priorities, effective 2025-10-09, including an education choice priority that covers state efforts such as tax-credit scholarships and education savings accounts.

Treasury releases guidance on the scholarship credit; a States Newsroom report says the IRS counts 30 states opted in, that governors in Hawaii, Minnesota, New Mexico and Oregon have said they will not participate, and that Democratic governors in Arizona and Wisconsin vetoed opt-in bills.

Treasury and the IRS publish temporary regulations (effective 2026-12-01, expiring 2029-10-01) for the scholarship credit under new Code section 25F, covering state opt-in and certification of scholarship-granting organizations; states must file the opt-in form by 2027-01-01 and their organization lists by 2027-02-15 for 2027.

Treasury and the IRS publish a companion proposed rule on the credit, with comments due 2026-12-01 and a public hearing on 2026-12-15; per the proposal the credit is capped at 1,700 dollars per individual taxpayer and scholarships are limited to households at or below 300 percent of area median income.

uncertainties: The count of 30 opted-in states comes from one States Newsroom report relaying the IRS, and an earlier ECS article counted 31 planning to opt in as of 2026-05-20 using a different tracker. The temporary regulations and the proposed rule were read through about the first 100,000 characters each, so details beyond that were not checked. The credit's terms ($1,700 cap, 300 percent of area median gross income, taxable years ending after 2026-12-31) are taken from the U.S. Code text at Cornell's Legal Information Institute (uscode.house.gov was under maintenance when fetched), as read through a fetch summary. ED's two letters on using Title I funds for school choice carry no issue date on the pages read (one last reviewed 2025-12-08, the other undated), so they are cited as sources but not placed on the timeline; whether they satisfied the 60-day deadline was not established. The Defense and Interior plans under Executive Order 14191 were not located; the D.C. program's FY2026 appropriation and any House or Senate action on H.R. 5181 after introduction were not checked. The enactment date of Public Law 119-21 is taken as 2025-07-04. Searches run: two web searches (state opt-in and D.C. program/ESA), one on ED guidance, and Federal Register queries for scholarship granting organization, education savings accounts, school choice, education freedom and Bureau of Indian Education.
